REVISE

- **minor** `packages/core/src/modules/promotions/api/codes/[id]/generated/route.ts:96` — The PR fixes offset-pagination instability in two list routes but only adds a regression test for `GET /api/workflows/portal/tasks`; The identical fix on `GET /api/promotions/codes/[id]/generated` has no test, so a future removal or reordering of the `id` tiebreaker there would go undetected while the portal route stays protected; Add a route-level unit test for the generated-codes list asserting the `orderBy` (e.g. in `packages/core/src/modules/promotions/api/__tests__/`), mirroring `portalTasks.route.test.ts`.

Re-review:

APPROVE

Reviewed head `9d3e00b9` vs `main` `fe9764f7`.

- The previous finding is addressed: `9d3e00b9` adds `packages/core/src/modules/promotions/api/__tests__/generated-codes-list.route.test.ts`, which drives the real `GET /api/promotions/codes/[id]/generated` handler and asserts `orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc', id: 'desc' }` with the page-2 offset. It fails against the old `{ createdAt: 'desc' }` ordering and passes with the fix, so it genuinely guards the tiebreaker. The added portal-list assertion (`orderBy: { createdAt: 'DESC', id: 'DESC' }`) covers the second route the same way.
- No new defects found: the diff is two one-line ordering additions plus the two tests, no API shape, schema or contract change, and the branch merges cleanly.
- Limitation: the head is a fork (`pcbeingused333`), so GitHub withholds its workflows (`action_required`); no required CI check has a result. The review checkout has no dependency install, so a narrow local Jest run was not possible either; the tests were verified statically against the route call site instead.
- Limitation: pending/absent CI is not a failure — this approval is a code-review verdict and branch protection remains authoritative for the merge.

@pcbeingused333 thanks — the generated-codes regression closes the remaining gap.
